reviewer_explanation: AI root cause matched the expected fault, confidence was justified by the evidence given, and next_command added real diagnostic value. No changes needed.

expected_fault: Fa0/8 was assigned to VLAN 10 instead of VLAN 30 by mistake, so the DHCP request is relayed using the VLAN 10 sub-interface's helper scope.
reviewer_explanation: AI root cause matched the expected fault, confidence was justified by the evidence given, and next_command added real diagnostic value. No changes needed.

expected_fault: The trunk's native VLAN is set to 1 on SW1 and 99 on SW2 — a mismatched native VLAN, which risks VLAN leakage for untagged frames.

ai_root_cause: PC2 has an incorrect default gateway. Its gateway is configured as 192.168.10.10, but the topology note states that the gateway should be 192.168.10.1.
expected_fault: Default gateway is typo'd as 192.168.10.10 instead of the router's actual interface address 192.168.10.1.
reviewer_explanation: AI root cause matched the expected fault, confidence was justified by the evidence given, and next_command added real diagnostic value. No changes needed.

ai_root_cause: The VLAN 10 SVI on SW1 is down/down, so it cannot provide gateway connectivity to hosts in VLAN 10. The output confirms the SVI is not operational, but does not identify why it is down.
expected_fault: SVI 'interface vlan 10' is administratively down (no shutdown missing), taking down the gateway for the whole VLAN.
reviewer_explanation: AI marked confidence as High but its own root_cause text admits it 'does not identify why it is down' -- that's an internal inconsistency. The raw evidence only shows Status: down / Protocol: down, not 'administratively down', so the shutdown cause isn't actually confirmed yet. Reviewer downgraded confidence to Medium and changed next_command to 'show running-config interface vlan10' to check for a shutdown statement before assuming that's the cause.

ai_root_cause: HSRP is in an inconsistent state because both R1 and R2 report themselves as Active for group 10. This can cause both routers to answer for the virtual gateway and produce intermittent gateway connectivity.
expected_fault: Both R1 and R2 report themselves as Active for HSRP group 10 (priority/preempt misconfiguration), causing an active/active split and intermittent gateway failures.
reviewer_explanation: AI root cause matched the expected fault, confidence was justified by the evidence given, and next_command added real diagnostic value. No changes needed.

ai_root_cause: The DHCP pool SALES_POOL has only five addresses available, from 192.168.10.10 to 192.168.10.14, and all five are already leased. New PCs therefore have no available address in this pool.
expected_fault: The DHCP pool's address range (only 5 usable addresses) is exhausted; the pool needs a larger range or the network/exclude statements corrected.
reviewer_explanation: AI root cause matched the expected fault, confidence was justified by the evidence given, and next_command added real diagnostic value. No changes needed.

ai_root_cause: The VLAN 20 router sub-interface has no DHCP relay configuration, so DHCP broadcasts from VLAN 20 cannot be forwarded to the DHCP server in VLAN 10.
expected_fault: 'ip helper-address' pointing at the DHCP server is missing on the VLAN 20 sub-interface, so DHCP broadcasts from VLAN 20 are never relayed to the server.
reviewer_explanation: AI root cause matched the expected fault, confidence was justified by the evidence given, and next_command added real diagnostic value. No changes needed.

ai_root_cause: The DHCP pool SALES_POOL does not provide a default gateway to clients. Without a default-router option, clients can receive an IP address and subnet mask but lack the gateway needed for inter-VLAN or internet access.
expected_fault: The DHCP pool has no 'default-router' statement, so clients never learn a gateway address even though addressing works.
reviewer_explanation: AI root cause matched the expected fault, confidence was justified by the evidence given, and next_command added real diagnostic value. No changes needed.

ai_root_cause: The configured DNS server 192.168.10.200 is unreachable from PC1, so DNS name resolution fails even though IP connectivity works.
expected_fault: The configured DNS server address (192.168.10.200) does not correspond to a real DNS server on the network, so all name resolution fails while raw IP connectivity works.
reviewer_explanation: Root cause is correct (wrong DNS server IP). But next_command just repeats the ping command whose result (4/4 lost) was already given as evidence -- it adds nothing new. Reviewer changed next_command to 'show ip dhcp binding' to confirm what DNS address clients are actually being handed, which is more useful for the actual fix.

ai_root_cause: ACL 110 is blocking DNS traffic from VLAN 10 by denying UDP traffic from 192.168.10.0/24 to destination port 53. The ACL is applied inbound on Gi0/0.10, affecting VLAN 10 only.
expected_fault: ACL 110 explicitly denies UDP port 53 (DNS) from VLAN 10 before the permit-any statement, blocking DNS queries only from that VLAN.
reviewer_explanation: AI root cause matched the expected fault, confidence was justified by the evidence given, and next_command added real diagnostic value. No changes needed.

ai_root_cause: R1 is configured to use only the public DNS server 8.8.8.8, so internal hostnames such as fileserver.corp.local cannot be resolved if they are hosted only on the internal DNS server.
expected_fault: Only the public DNS server is configured under 'ip name-server'; the internal DNS server that holds the corp.local zone was never added, so internal names cannot resolve.
reviewer_explanation: AI root cause matched the expected fault, confidence was justified by the evidence given, and next_command added real diagnostic value. No changes needed.

ai_root_cause: R1 has no route to the remote branch subnet 172.16.5.0/24, so VLAN 10 hosts cannot reach that network. The routing table shows only directly connected HQ networks and the serial link.
expected_fault: R1 has no static route (or dynamic routing) for 172.16.5.0/24 via the branch link, so packets to the branch subnet are dropped at R1.
reviewer_explanation: AI root cause matched the expected fault, confidence was justified by the evidence given, and next_command added real diagnostic value. No changes needed.

ai_root_cause: R1 and R2 have mismatched OSPF areas on the Serial0/0/0 link. R1 uses Area 0 while R2 uses Area 1, preventing an OSPF adjacency from forming.
expected_fault: R1 advertises the shared link in area 0 while R2 advertises it in area 1 — mismatched OSPF area IDs prevent adjacency from forming.
reviewer_explanation: AI root cause matched the expected fault, confidence was justified by the evidence given, and next_command added real diagnostic value. No changes needed.

ai_root_cause: R1's OSPF configuration does not include the 192.168.30.0/24 network, so VLAN 30 is not being advertised through OSPF to R2.
expected_fault: The OSPF 'network' statement for 192.168.30.0/24 is missing, so that interface is never advertised into OSPF even though it is up.
reviewer_explanation: AI root cause matched the expected fault, confidence was justified by the evidence given, and next_command added real diagnostic value. No changes needed.

ai_root_cause: R1 has no default route for unknown destinations, so internal traffic can work while internet-bound traffic has no route toward the ISP.
expected_fault: There is no default route (0.0.0.0/0) pointing to the ISP, so internally-routed traffic has no path out to unknown external destinations.
reviewer_explanation: AI root cause matched the expected fault, confidence was justified by the evidence given, and next_command added real diagnostic value. No changes needed.

ai_root_cause: The static route to 172.16.5.0/24 via the direct serial link is not selected because the routing table prefers the OSPF route only if the static route is not actually installed. The output is internally inconsistent because a static route with administrative distance 1 should normally be preferred over OSPF distance 110, so the exact reason requires further confirmation.
expected_fault: The OSPF-learned route (AD 110) is not actually preferred here because a redistribution/metric issue is letting the higher-AD path win in this topology; the static route's administrative distance and redistribution metrics need to be reviewed so the direct link is preferred.
reviewer_explanation: This is the intentionally ambiguous case in the set. The AI's answer was actually well reasoned -- it correctly flagged the routing table as internally inconsistent and kept confidence at Medium rather than guessing. Reviewer still flags this for a required manual lab check before applying the suggested 'remove or correct the conflicting route' fix, since acting on an unconfirmed cause here could break a currently-working path.

ai_root_cause: ACL 101 has a broad deny statement for all IP traffic from 192.168.20.0/24 before the specific HTTPS permit statement, so the explicitly permitted traffic is blocked by the earlier rule.
expected_fault: A broad 'deny ip any' style statement (line 10) sits above the intended permit statement (line 20), so the permit is never reached and all VLAN 20 traffic is dropped.
reviewer_explanation: AI root cause matched the expected fault, confidence was justified by the evidence given, and next_command added real diagnostic value. No changes needed.

ai_root_cause: ACL 105 is applied inbound on Gi0/1, but the ACL is intended to filter traffic leaving Gi0/1 toward the ISP. Therefore, outbound traffic does not pass through the ACL in the intended direction.
expected_fault: ACL 105 is applied 'in' on the ISP-facing interface (filtering inbound internet traffic) instead of 'out', so it never inspects outbound traffic from internal hosts as intended.
reviewer_explanation: Root cause and fix direction are correct (ACL applied in instead of out). next_command just re-displays the interface config already shown in the evidence. Reviewer changed it to 'show access-lists 105' so the next step actually inspects the ACL rules themselves.

ai_root_cause: ACL 102 contains a deny for host 192.168.10.50 to the server, but no explicit permit statement follows. The implicit deny at the end of the ACL therefore blocks all other traffic that reaches ACL 102.
expected_fault: Only a deny statement was written; with no explicit 'permit ip any any' after it, the ACL's implicit deny-all drops every other host's traffic too.
reviewer_explanation: AI root cause matched the expected fault, confidence was justified by the evidence given, and next_command added real diagnostic value. No changes needed.

ai_root_cause: ACL 130 is applied inbound on the VLAN 10 sub-interface instead of the intended VLAN 30 sub-interface. Therefore, VLAN 30 guest traffic does not pass through ACL 130.
expected_fault: ACL 130 was applied to the VLAN 10 sub-interface instead of the VLAN 30 (guest) sub-interface it was designed for, so guest traffic is never filtered.
reviewer_explanation: AI root cause matched the expected fault, confidence was justified by the evidence given, and next_command added real diagnostic value. No changes needed.

ai_root_cause: PAT/NAT overload is not configured, so internal traffic has no source translation when accessing the internet. The inside and outside interfaces are marked for NAT, but there is no ip nat inside source list ... overload statement.

reviewer_explanation: AI root cause matched the expected fault, confidence was justified by the evidence given, and next_command added real diagnostic value. No changes needed.

ai_root_cause: NAT translations are not occurring because the inside and outside interfaces are not marked with ip nat inside and ip nat outside. The overload statement alone is insufficient without correct NAT interface roles.
expected_fault: Neither interface has been marked with 'ip nat inside' or 'ip nat outside', so the router never applies the otherwise-correct NAT overload rule to any traffic.
reviewer_explanation: AI root cause matched the expected fault, confidence was justified by the evidence given, and next_command added real diagnostic value. No changes needed.

ai_root_cause: The static NAT rule maps public 203.0.113.10:80 to the wrong internal address, 192.168.10.99. The actual web server is 192.168.10.100, so outside traffic is forwarded to the wrong host.
expected_fault: The static NAT entry maps the public address to 192.168.10.99, but the real web server is 192.168.10.100 — a wrong internal (local) address in the mapping.
reviewer_explanation: Root cause is correct (wrong internal IP in the static NAT mapping). next_command repeats the same 'show run' line already quoted as evidence. Reviewer changed it to 'show ip nat translations' so the next step verifies live translations after the fix is applied, rather than re-reading the same config line.

ai_root_cause: NAT ACL 1 only permits the VLAN 10 subnet, so VLAN 20 traffic is not included in the set of inside addresses eligible for NAT translation.
